hero.subline: Finance and data. I build a single source of data and a reporting layer that finance and commercial teams trust and use.
hero.body: I have spent about eight years in Big 4 advisory, government analytics and corporate FP&A. At World Kinect I worked with the finance team to put management reporting for 25 legal entities on one governed source. Manual extracts and reconciliations gave way to automated pipelines, and the report went from 10 days after month-end close to a daily refresh.
hero.status: Based in Oslo. Open to permanent roles in Norway and selected project work.

25-legal-entities.title: 25 legal entities, one reporting layer
25-legal-entities.label: World Kinect, Senior FP&A Analyst
25-legal-entities.summary: Management reporting for 25 legal entities now refreshes daily from one governed source, instead of 10 days after close.
25-legal-entities.role: Senior FP&A Analyst, World Kinect, Oslo, Dec 2023 to Jul 2026
25-legal-entities.context: A group with 25 legal entities across APAC, EMEA and North America. Its data sat in three CRMs, two ERPs and two contract management systems. Management reports arrived about 10 days after month-end close. The numbers were pulled by hand from the systems, then reconciled manually. My work covered the renewable energy side, long-term energy contracts and the US gas business.
did: Designed the data model and built the integration layer, together with the finance team, that brought those systems into one governed reporting platform.
Python ingestion into Snowflake, medallion-style data layers, data marts for Power BI.
Defined master data standards. Traced reporting discrepancies to their root cause and fixed them in the data model, not in the reports.
Only part of the group sat in Oracle FCCS, so I built a separate consolidation and reporting layer in Snowflake covering the full entity perimeter.
Automated reconciliations and re-engineered the month-end close and variance analysis workflows.
Replaced Excel-based processes with BI reporting embedded in existing leadership routines.

Built a time tracker and rolled it out to the consulting department, including training the people who use it. Before, the department set project completion by estimate. Now logged hours drive the revenue accruals automatically and show profitability by client.
25-legal-entities.myRoleText: I built the data model, pipelines, dashboards and the time tracker, and trained its users. My manager handled communication with the commercial teams.
result: Management reporting moved from 10 days after close to a daily refresh.
Extracts from several systems and manual reconciliations were replaced by one governed source.
Management P&L by entity, region and business line, drillable to transaction level and tying to the statutory accounts.
Revenue accruals for consulting projects come from logged time instead of estimates, and profitability by client is visible.

sales-funnel.title: A B2B funnel the bank can manage
sales-funnel.label: MAIB Bank, Product Owner
sales-funnel.summary: I led the team that built the B2B customer funnel for Moldova's largest commercial bank, with the reasons for drop-off. The funnel became manageable.
sales-funnel.role: Product Owner, CRM & B2B Marketing Analytics, MAIB Bank, Chisinau (remote from Oslo), Nov 2022 to Dec 2023
sales-funnel.context: MAIB is Moldova's largest commercial bank. It had no unified view of the customer journey, from marketing spend to sales conversion.
did: Owned the Lead module within the CRM platform.
Led a cross-functional team of 5 with full agile delivery.
With the team, designed the end-to-end B2B funnel from marketing spend to sales conversion and recorded the reason for drop-off at each stage.
Built the funnel logic and the data collection layer that fed a unified model and a dashboard.
result: The first unified customer journey tracking at the bank.
The funnel became manageable: the team could see where B2B customers dropped out and why.

cahul-map.title: A city map for investment decisions
cahul-map.label: Cahul, two-person team
cahul-map.summary: One map of Cahul's master plan, cadastre, council decisions and transport documents, every answer linked to its source page.
cahul-map.role: Cahul, Moldova, a two-person development team, live
cahul-map.context: The current task is to help the city reach its goal of a more efficient transport network, and to make urban planning more transparent and faster.
did: Brought the master plan, cadastre, council decisions, strategies and transport documents onto one map. Click a parcel or a street to see what is allowed and planned there, with a link to the source page.
Built first models on the data: population, trips and the public transport network, so options can be compared and checked against regulations.
Added Now and Plan states for layers and a network editor, as the base for a digital twin of the city.
result: A public site in Romanian, Russian and English, live at cahulmap.pages.dev.
The current transport network compared with several optimized options.
In demo mode: what can be built where. Until now this was available only by request to the city hall, within several weeks.

speak-to-data.title: Speak to data: ask the dashboard
speak-to-data.label: Own project, in development
speak-to-data.summary: Ask the dashboard a question and get the answer in real time, from validated numbers. Get an automatic commentary on the report after period close. Built on a KPI dashboard for the SaaS industry (rule40).
speak-to-data.context: I have built dashboards from single pages to large semantic models. The larger the organization, the more complex the questions it needs answered. A dashboard shows the agreed numbers, and follow-up questions usually go to an analyst. This project gives the dashboard an analyst of its own: the user asks a question and gets the answer in real time. I am building it on a KPI dashboard for the SaaS industry.
did: First the semantic model and the metrics in dbt, with tests.
Then a chat on the front end: a plain-language question becomes a call to a deterministic dbt metric, and the answer comes back in plain language.
At period close, the model writes a text summary of the report and answers questions on any detail. Useful for companies with a branching hierarchy, to see where attention is needed.
Metrics are versioned YAML contracts and staged by company stage, not one Rule of 40 number.
result: The model handles language, never arithmetic. I can demo it live.
